confidence_analysis.characterization: Predominantly low-to-moderate confidence borderline errors (Group B mean conf = 56.4%, Group D mean conf = 61.2% vs Group A mean conf = 80.2%). Over 38% of CLEAR->DROP errors have confidence < 50%.

top_distinguishing_features.observation: DROP decelerates sharply across frames H+5..H+11, yielding significantly lower late/early velocity ratio than CLEAR.
CLEAR is struck slightly deeper in the rearcourt (mean Y=620 vs 585 for DROP). CLEAR->DROP errors occur when CLEAR is hit shallower (mean Y=598).
CLEAR possesses slightly higher vertical launch angle than DROP, but substantial overlap remains.

non_deployable_oracle_findings.note: CLEAR and DROP separate almost perfectly at landing (mean Landing Y = 745 vs 285). However, this information is strictly non-deployable at impact time.

court_zone_findings.conclusion: The DROP/CLEAR confusion is heavily concentrated in the Rearcourt, where 86.7% of CLEAR->DROP errors (98/113) and 89.0% of DROP->CLEAR errors (65/73) reside.

contact_overhead_findings.conclusion: Over 97% of both CLEAR and DROP strokes are overhead shots (hit_height==2). Overhead mechanics provide virtually zero discriminative signal.

primary_failure_mode: Temporal observation window limitation combined with disguised rearcourt overhead mechanics. Within 11 post-impact frames (Window C), players' swing preparation and initial shuttle launch angle for sliced drops and high clears overlap significantly. Deceleration cues only begin emerging around frames H+8..H+11.
recommended_next_experiment: EXP_DROP_CLEAR_02: Targeted post-impact visual deceleration feature or pairwise auxiliary CLEAR/DROP boundary loss operating on late Window C frames without modifying frozen base representations.
